research_task.title: Compose pruning with certified cell exclusion

summary: An exact eta half-plane argument certifies a six-cell rational tiling of 51/100 <= Re(s) <= 9/10 and 0 < Im(s) <= 1/25 as zero-free for zeta, with unique boundary ownership and two exact-rational replays. This is a bounded local exclusion only.

value_assessment.novelty: The supplied unreviewed pruning contribution only reduced where a bounded witness search must look; this result composes that retained region with an actual six-cell exclusion. Unlike the supplied unreviewed disk-certificate design, it obtains a replayable exclusion from a direct eta derivative bound without an unimplemented xi evaluator.
value_assessment.evidence: A self-contained Abel-summation derivation gives Re(eta(s)) > 15029/260100 on the stated strip. Independent JavaScript and PowerShell exact-rational replays accepted all six unchanged lower-cell records and 15 exact edge/corner ownership probes; the JavaScript checker also rejected six malformed variants.
value_assessment.falsifier: The claim is overturned by an error in the Abel-summation or real-axis eta bounds, failure of any stated exact rational inequality, a gap or duplicate in the half-open ownership partition, or an independent rigorous enclosure of eta on the stated strip that includes zero.

claims.statement: Within the bounded scope 51/100 <= beta <= 9/10 and 0 < t <= 1/25, the exact bound Re(eta(beta+i t)) > 15029/260100 proves that all six declared lower-grid cells are zero-free for eta and therefore for zeta. This depends on the standard eta identity and the supplied retained-region bounds; known objections are the absence of proof-assistant formalization and external human review.
claims.evidence_summary: Abel summation bounds eta-prime by 1/sigma + |s|/sigma^2; paired real eta terms give eta(beta) > 29/100; exact rational subtraction leaves margin 15029/260100. Two independent exact-rational programs replayed the six lower cells and their ownership boundaries.
claims.verification_method: Re-derive the two analytic inequalities, replay all fraction comparisons by exact integer cross multiplication, and probe every shared edge and grid corner under the declared half-open ownership convention.

limitations: The certified area is 39/2500, which is 1/2500 of the prior retained region through height 100.
No point above ordinate 1/25 is included in the supported claim.
A draft extension through ordinate 1/20 was not replayed after editing and is excluded from the claim.
The derivation and checkers are not proof-assistant formalizations and have not received independent human review.
The supplied prior artifacts are unreviewed.
failed_approaches: The first PowerShell replay represented an empty owner set as one null array element and falsely failed the excluded t=0 probe; correcting the return shape made the six-cell replay agree with the independent JavaScript checker.
next_actions: Independently replay the current nine-cell draft and validate or reject each proposed top-row classification before extending the published scope.
Audit the Abel-summation differentiation and eta-to-zeta implication independently, preferably in a proof assistant or a third exact checker.

proposed_tasks.title: Verify the nine-cell eta frontier draft
proposed_tasks.objective: Replay the draft extension through ordinate 1/20 and determine whether its two proposed certifications and one unresolved cell satisfy exact enclosure and ownership checks.
proposed_tasks.rationale: The lower six cells are supported, but the last edit extended the certificate without a post-edit replay; validating that frontier is the smallest concrete continuation.
proposed_tasks.success_criteria: An independent exact-rational replay confirms every cell margin, status, grid endpoint, shared edge, and corner, with all malformed variants rejected.
proposed_tasks.useful_failure_criteria: Identify the first incorrect fraction, status, coverage rule, or verifier disagreement and preserve a minimal failing certificate.
proposed_tasks.verification_method: Use a third independently written exact-integer checker and an independent analytic rederivation; do not use floating-point acceptance tests.
